$comment: Source of truth for this site's AWS Amplify redirect rules.
Amplify has NO repo-level redirect file. customHttp.yml sets headers only;
redirects live in the app's customRules.
Do NOT pass this file to --custom-rules: that flag wants a bare array of
rules, and this file is an object carrying $comment and $why annotations.
Run scripts/amplify-redirects/check.sh instead. It reads the live rules
(read-only — only the amplify:GetApp the preview role already has), diffs
them against this file, writes the apply-ready array with the annotations
stripped, and prints the exact command.
Applying REPLACES the entire rule set, so this file must list every rule the
app should have, not just the ones being added.
Applied by hand, deliberately. Automating it would need amplify:UpdateApp on
the app ARN, which also grants control of the build spec and environment
variables — the preview role is scoped read-only at app level precisely so a
PR-triggered workflow cannot reach production config. A handful of rules that
change a few times a year does not justify that escalation.
Wildcards are Amplify's <*> syntax, not :splat. Order matters: Amplify
evaluates top to bottom and stops at the first match, so specific rules go
above the wildcards that would otherwise swallow them.

rules.$why: Retired Spotify content adaptor. Ported from netlify.toml, which the site has never read — it deploys via Amplify.
Same, for the per-artist pages beneath it.
